original.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, passed by Parliament in August 2026:
items: It mandates that mediation in delayed-payment disputes must be completed within 90 days.
If a buyer's challenge to an arbitral award is pending for more than six months, courts must release at least 50 per cent of the awarded amount to the MSE supplier.
It raises the share of an arbitral award that a buyer must deposit with the court when challenging it from 50 per cent to 75 per cent.
original.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
original.explain: Statement 3 is wrong: buyers already had to deposit 75 per cent of an award, but its release to the supplier was left to judicial discretion. The bill adds a floor of 50 per cent release once a challenge has been pending for over six months.
original.source: Now, if the challenge sits pending for more than six months, courts must release at least 50 per cent of the awarded amount to the MSE supplier upfront.

rewritten.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, passed by Parliament in August 2026:
items: It mandates that mediation in delayed-payment disputes must be completed within 90 days.
If a buyer's challenge to an arbitral award is pending for more than six months, courts must release at least 50 per cent of the awarded amount to the MSE supplier.
Even before the amendment, a buyer challenging an arbitral award had to deposit 75 per cent of it with the court, but its release to the supplier was left to judicial discretion.
rewritten.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
rewritten.explain: All three statements are correct: the bill mandates that mediation be completed within 90 days and adds a floor of 50 per cent release once a challenge has been pending for over six months. The 75 per cent deposit requirement already existed, but release of that money was previously at judicial discretion.
rewritten.source: Buyers challenging an arbitral award already had to deposit 75 per cent of it with the court, but release of that money to the supplier was left to judicial discretion.
